newsitem.title: POLAND: Swarzedz Sept loss due to provisions.
newsitem.headline: Swarzedz Sept loss due to provisions.

text.p: Polish furniture maker Swarzedzkie Fabryki Mebli Swarzedz SA (Swarzedz) made a September net loss of 28.5 million zlotys after making provisions largely for receivables, the firm's president said.
"It's questionable whether we'll get that money back," Julian Nuckowski said after a news conference on Friday.
Nuckowski was appointed acting chief executive in June and full CEO in August after the company's supervisory board approved a restructuring programme and the previous president stepped down.
Swarzedz spokesman Sebastian Szczesny told Reuters the receivables represented furniture tranferred to subsidiary trade firms for which the parent had yet to receive payment.
The September loss put Swarzedz's loss for the first three quarters of this year at 34.1 million zlotys.

Nuckowski said that Swarzedz had been advised by its auditor Deloitte & Touche to up receivable provisions to 17 million zlotys from the previous 0.4 million, and that total provisions of 22.9 million zlotys included warranty and other claims.

The audit was requested by the firm's main creditors, Polish Development Bank (PBR), Bank Gdanski and Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy (PBG), which in late July agreed that Swarzedz should stop debt payments for three months.
Nuckowski said financial costs were eating 13 percent of Swarzedz's sales revenue.
Swarzedz's sales of 9.7 million zlotys in September lifted the year's total to 75.7 million zlotys.
Nuckowski said Swarzedz would make an operational profit in the fourth quarter and that its net loss for the whole year should end around the current loss for nine months.
He said the firm might issue shares or convertible bonds by the end of February, which could go in a debt-for-equity swap, and was mulling a joint venture with a Western partner.

He said all of the firm's present production was based on orders, that it had taken out no loans since July and was drastically cutting jobs and the number of firms in its holding, cutting its number of distributors to five from 24.
Nuckowski also said the firm was preparing a longer-term restructuring scheme for 1997-1998.
